word_readings.name: printable runs
word_readings.definition: Maximal runs of non-whitespace containing at least one character printable in the C locale. This is what GNU wc -w returns when LC_ALL=C: a token made only of an em dash, an arrow or a ≤ sign never opens a word.

word_readings.name: whitespace runs
word_readings.definition: Maximal runs of non-whitespace, full stop. What the same GNU wc -w returns when LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, and what almost every word-count snippet computes.

word_readings.name: UAX#29 word-like
word_readings.definition: Segments the platform's ICU marks word-like under the default word boundaries of Unicode Standard Annex #29 §4.1 — conformance clause UAX29-C2-1. Hyphenated compounds become two words; markdown asterisks stop being part of one.

word_readings.name: UAX#29 word-like, letters only
word_readings.definition: W3 with segments that contain no letter dropped, so a bare year or count is not a word. A declared profile in the sense of UAX29-C2-2, declared here.

word_readings.name: rendered prose
word_readings.definition: Markdown syntax removed and a digest's leading editorial note removed, then whitespace runs: what someone reads off the page rather than out of the file.

line_readings.name: stored lines
line_readings.definition: Newline characters in the file, which is what wc -l counts and what a diff calls a line.

line_readings.name: stored lines with something on them
line_readings.definition: The same, with blank lines not counted.

line_readings.name: rendered at a width, breaking at spaces
line_readings.definition: Each stored line wrapped greedily at the chosen column, breaking only after a space; a token longer than the width is broken at the width, as a terminal does.

line_readings.name: rendered at a width, breaking at spaces and joiners
line_readings.definition: P1, additionally allowing a break after a hyphen, a dash, a slash, a closing bracket or an arrow — a declared subset of the tailorable rules of UAX#14 §6.2, disclosed here as UAX14-C1 requires of any tailoring, and not a conforming implementation of that algorithm.
